title: Procedural Timeline Multi-Track Keyframe Editor
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js that implements a procedural timeline multi-track keyframe editor controlling 3D animated objects in a scene.

## Scene Setup
- Use Three.js with a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 5, 12) looking at the origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and a directional light at (5, 10, 7) with intensity 0.8.
- Create a ground plane (20x20, gray, receiveShadow) at y=0.
- Create 3 animated objects in the scene:
  - Track 0: A red Box (1x1x1) starting at position (-4, 0.5, 0), named 'RedCube'
  - Track 1: A green Sphere (radius 0.6) starting at position (0, 0.6, 0), named 'GreenSphere'
  - Track 2: A blue Cylinder (radiusTop 0.4, radiusBottom 0.4, height 1.5) starting at position (4, 0.75, 0), named 'BlueCylinder'
- Enable shadows on the renderer.

## Timeline UI (DOM Overlay)
- Create a DOM-based timeline panel fixed at the bottom of the screen, height 220px, full width, dark background (#1a1a2e).
- The timeline has:
  - A top toolbar row with: Play/Pause button (id='btn-play'), Stop button (id='btn-stop'), a current-time display (id='time-display'), a total-duration input (id='duration-input', default 5.0 seconds), and a playback-speed selector (id='speed-select') with options 0.25x, 0.5x, 1x, 2x.
  - Below the toolbar, 3 horizontal track lanes (one per object), each 50px tall, labeled on the left with the object name. Each track lane has id='track-0', 'track-1', 'track-2'.
  - A vertical red playhead line (id='playhead') that moves across the timeline during playback and can be dragged horizontally to scrub time.
  - The timeline ruler area (id='timeline-ruler') shows tick marks every 0.5 seconds.

## Keyframe System
- Each track stores keyframes. A keyframe records: time (seconds), position {x,y,z}, rotation {x,y,z} (Euler in radians), and scale {x,y,z}.
- Each object starts with a default keyframe at t=0 with its initial transform.
- Clicking on a track lane at a horizontal position inserts a new keyframe at that time for that track. Keyframes appear as small diamond shapes (CSS) on the track lane with class 'keyframe-marker'.
- The currently selected keyframe is highlighted in yellow. Selecting a keyframe populates an edit panel.
- A keyframe property editor panel (id='keyframe-editor') appears on the right side (or as a floating panel) when a keyframe is selected, showing numeric inputs for posX, posY, posZ, rotX, rotY, rotZ, scaleX, scaleY, scaleZ (ids: 'kf-posX', 'kf-posY', 'kf-posZ', 'kf-rotX', 'kf-rotY', 'kf-rotZ', 'kf-scaleX', 'kf-scaleY', 'kf-scaleZ').
- Changing values in the editor updates the selected keyframe and the 3D object preview immediately.
- A Delete Keyframe button (id='btn-delete-kf') removes the selected keyframe (cannot delete the t=0 keyframe).

## Interpolation & Playback
- During playback, each object's transform is interpolated between its keyframes using linear interpolation (lerp for position/scale, slerp-like for rotation).
- Pressing Play starts the animation from the current playhead time. The playhead advances in real-time (scaled by speed). When it reaches the end (duration), it loops back to 0.
- Pressing Stop resets playhead to 0 and resets all objects to their t=0 keyframe transforms.
- The time-display updates every frame during playback showing current time to 2 decimal places.

## Keyboard Shortcuts
- Spacebar: toggle play/pause
- 'S' key: stop (reset to 0)
- Delete/Backspace: delete selected keyframe
- Left/Right arrow: nudge playhead by 0.1 seconds

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- isPlaying: boolean
- currentTime: number (current playhead time in seconds)
- duration: number (total timeline duration)
- playbackSpeed: number
- selectedTrack: number or null (0, 1, 2)
- selectedKeyframeIndex: number or null
- tracks: array of 3 objects, each with:
  - name: string
  - keyframes: array of {time, position:{x,y,z}, rotation:{x,y,z}, scale:{x,y,z}}
- objects: array of 3 objects each with:
  - name: string
  - position: {x, y, z}
  - rotation: {x, y, z}
  - scale: {x, y, z}
- totalKeyframeCount: number (sum of all keyframes across all tracks)
- loopCount: number (how many times playback has looped)

Update window.__3D_STATE__ every frame in the animation loop to reflect the true current state of the scene and timeline.
physics_constraints: Interpolated positions must remain NaN-free at all times. Scale components must never be zero or negative. Keyframes within a track must remain sorted by time. currentTime must always be in [0, duration]. Playhead position must be proportional to currentTime/duration.
